handbookNote: Rhode Island Commercial Driver License Manual (base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System' content, Version: July 2014, front-matter copyright-stamped 'COPYRIGHT (c) 2025 AAMVA' on the reprint page despite the body text consistently reading 'Version: July 2014' throughout -- treated as a reprint/redistribution copyright stamp on otherwise-unchanged July 2014 content, not a substantive revision, consistent with how this project has resolved similar cover-vs-body version mismatches in other states), published by the Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles (RI DMV) -- fetched directly from https://dmv.ri.gov/media/2966/download?language=en on 2026-08-23 (4.8MB PDF, linked as 'Commercial Driver License Manual - Modernized Version' from the official Operator Manuals page at dmv.ri.gov/licenses-permits-ids/permits-tests/operator-manuals and the Commercial Driving License (CDL) page at dmv.ri.gov/licenses-permits-ids/commercial/commercial-driving-license-cdl, checked 2026-08-23), full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ri_cdl_research/ri_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,387 lines. Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are FULLY CONFIRMED, directly from Rhode Island's own official manual text (Knowledge Testing Instructions, front matter) -- an explicit chart titled 'Test / Total Questions / Needed to Pass / Passing Percentage' states: General Knowledge 50 questions/40 to pass/80%; Air Brakes 25/20/80%; Combination 20/16/80%; Tankers 20/16/80%; Passenger 20/16/80%; Doubles/Triples 20/16/80%; Hazardous Materials 30/24/80%; School Bus 20/16/80%. This is a direct quote from an official RI.gov-hosted document, not hedged or inferred, and matches the federal 80% minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a). Additional confirmed RI-specific mechanics: CDL transactions are performed only at the CDL Office in the Cranston DMV (600 New London Avenue), by appointment, 8:30am-2:00pm; only one exam type may be taken per day, starting with General Knowledge; a failed test requires a 5-business-day wait before retaking; passing scores are banked and do not need to be retaken; all tests are given electronically, with manual (written) tests used only on system failure; a CLP is valid for a maximum of one year and cannot be renewed (all knowledge tests must be retaken if it expires); a CLP must be held at least 14 days before the skills test; ELDT (Entry Level Driver Training) must be completed before skills testing or before the Hazardous Materials Endorsement knowledge test, for first-time Class A/B CDLs, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time school bus/passenger/hazmat endorsement. Rhode Island uses the standard federal three-class system: Class A (combination, GCWR/GCW 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs, requires General Knowledge + Combination + Air Brakes + all skills tests), Class B (single vehicle 26,001+ lbs GVWR/GVW, requires General Knowledge + Combination test, with the L/no-air-brakes restriction applied unless the Air Brakes test is also passed), and Class C (does not meet A/B definition but is designed for 16+ passengers including driver, or hauls placarded hazmat -- requires the Passenger or Hazmat endorsement test plus skills tests for Passenger/School Bus only). Endorsement codes: T (Double/Triple Trailers, knowledge only), P (Passenger, knowledge + skills, requires a completed chauffeur application), N (Tank Vehicle, knowledge only), H (Hazardous Materials, TSA fingerprint-based threat assessment required), X (combined Tank + Hazmat, knowledge only), S (School Bus, knowledge + skills, requires a separate RI School Bus Certificate through the DMV School Bus Safety Office first) -- Rhode Island does not use a separate charter-bus 'C' endorsement. Only three endorsements are allowed on a CLP: P, S, and N (each with usage restrictions -- e.g., an N-endorsed CLP holder may only operate an empty, unpurged tank vehicle). Restriction codes confirmed from the manual's own table: L/Z (no full air-brake-system vehicles, applied if the Air Brakes test isn't passed or the skills test isn't taken in an air-brake vehicle), E (no manual-transmission vehicles, if the skills test was taken in an automatic), O (no fifth-wheel-connection Class A vehicles, if the skills test used a pintle-hook/non-fifth-wheel vehicle), M (Class A CDL holder who obtained a passenger/school-bus endorsement in a Class B vehicle -- restricted to Class B/C passenger vehicles only), N (Class B CDL holder who obtained a passenger/school-bus endorsement in a Class C vehicle -- restricted to Class C passenger vehicles only), V (FMCSA-notified medical variance, noted on the CDLIS record). One RI-specific quirk preserved rather than smoothed over: the manual's own worked knowledge-test example shows only three answer choices (a/b/c) on RI's actual computer-based CDL exam UI ('touch option c on the screen... or click on it'), unlike this project's standard four-choice (A/B/C/D) practice-question format; this question bank still uses the project's standard 4-choice format per established convention across all other CDL-track states, since the practice app's own UI/scoring is 4-choice regardless of what any single state's live proctored exam interface happens to render. Content-depth rationale: Rhode Island uses the same AAMVA-authored '2005 CDL Testing System' base manual (Version: July 2014) used by several earlier-vintage CDL-track states in this project, organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (combined with RI-specific front matter into the licensing bucket), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.8 the Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket. Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 22 questions, Tank Vehicles: 19, Doubles/Triples: 26, Passenger: 28) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (126 questions across two buckets), Hazardous Materials (138 questions across two buckets), Air Brakes (65), School Bus (68), Combination Vehicles (55), and Vehicle Inspection (55) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than an artificial per-bucket target. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Rhode Island manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds, tire tread depth minimums, hazmat placard weight/size thresholds, school bus danger-zone distances, railroad-crossing stopping distances, tank surge/outage figures, CDL exam question counts) were verified against the actual Rhode Island text read during drafting, independently re-verified by the top-level agent against the source text and JSON structure for every one of the 14 bucket files (including a full rebuild of one bucket's answer-letter balance after an initial draft skewed to 56.8% on a single letter -- fixed via a content-preserving choice-position rebalance, with every corrected question's explanation re-checked against its new correct_choice).
